Public production response headers, TTFB, and ten asset bodies were then checked separately; production real-user timings were not measured.

summary.gzipMeasurement: Offline compression experiment on local text and GLB files. Actual deployment Content-Encoding has not been inspected.
findings: The default CNRS role creates the 3D tour iframe on startup.
Tour initialization awaits the city model, then Earth/Europe textures, then the secondary mark before ready.
Main content is inserted by site.js; initial rendering and WebGL initialization share the main thread.
Twenty-five classic scripts load on every main-page visit, including Halloween geometry and chess code.
Robot models have uncompressed geometry and no Draco/Meshopt extensions; the custom loaders currently expect ordinary GLB attributes.
PDFs and chess-engine binaries were not requested by the default homepage.
Main 3D header already pauses when offscreen; further visibility gating should focus on the iframe and unnecessary startup work.

recommendations.action: Render the main text and an existing lightweight still first; initialize the letterhead and tour in stages after that paint.
Load the 7.39 MB tour on demand or after the page is usable; load each chapter and its planet textures when needed.
Simplify the 4.82 MB letterhead robot meshes while preserving joint nodes; add mesh-compression decoder support if applying Draco/Meshopt.
Verify production Brotli/gzip and cache headers. Offline gzip on the requested text/GLB bodies reduced about 15.09 MB to 7.99 MB.
Split Halloween geometry, Christmas caps, and chess scripts from the default startup path.
